evals.prompt: Write the cell for my Snowflake notebook that trains the confirmed Kumo churn model and publishes it to the model registry in ML.REGISTRY as CHURN_MODEL version V3. `model_plan`, `training_table` and `snapshot` are already defined in the notebook. I will run the cell myself.
evals.expected_output: Writes code that publishes during the fit: `trainer.fit(training_table, snapshot=snapshot, export_config=kumo.ModelOutputConfig(connector=registry_connector, location=kumo.ModelRegistryLocation(model_name='CHURN_MODEL', version='V3')))` with a connector scoped to ML.REGISTRY, then checks `training_result.published_model` and raises if it is None. Uses `location`, not `path`, for Snowflake. Checks that V3 does not already exist first and does not overwrite an existing version.
assertions: The code passes a kumo.ModelOutputConfig as export_config to trainer.fit
The code uses kumo.ModelRegistryLocation with model_name CHURN_MODEL and version V3
The code uses location= rather than path= for the Snowflake registry
The code checks training_result.published_model and treats None as a failure
The code checks that version V3 does not already exist and does not overwrite an existing version

evals.prompt: Load CHURN_MODEL from our Snowflake model registry in ML.REGISTRY and score new customers. SHOW VERSIONS lists V1, V2 and V3.
evals.expected_output: Several versions exist and the user named none, so it asks which version to load rather than choosing one. It explains that `version=None` loads the registry default, which is not necessarily the newest, and that 'latest' would mean the newest created_on, passed explicitly. It does not retrain.
assertions: Asks which version to load instead of picking one
Explains that loading without a version uses the registry default, not necessarily the newest
Does not train a new model

evals.prompt: Write the notebook cells that load version V2 of CHURN_MODEL from the Snowflake registry ML.REGISTRY and score our customers as of 2026-12-01. The V2 training record's graph-building code is in `build_graph_v2()`, already defined in the notebook. I will run the cells myself.
evals.expected_output: Writes code that restores with `kumo.Trainer.load_from_connector(registry_connector, location=kumo.ModelRegistryLocation(model_name='CHURN_MODEL', version='V2'))`, rebuilds the graph with the V2 training record's `build_graph_v2()` (not the live schema), creates a fresh `graph.snapshot()`, generates the prediction table with a naive `prediction_time` and `plan=loaded.training_table_generation_plan`, and predicts with `snapshot=` and an explicit binary threshold. No retraining.
assertions: The code loads with kumo.Trainer.load_from_connector and an explicit ModelRegistryLocation for version V2
The code rebuilds the graph from the V2 training record (build_graph_v2) rather than from the live schema or another version
The code builds a new graph.snapshot() for scoring
The code passes plan=loaded.training_table_generation_plan to generate_prediction_table
The code passes snapshot= to predict and an explicit binary classification threshold
The code does not call fit

evals.prompt: Write the cell for my Snowflake notebook that keeps my Kumo run's aggregate metrics and the per-trial validation results on the internal stage @ML.ARTIFACTS before the notebook shuts down, so I can look at them next week. The run's directory is `run_dir`, already defined. I will run the cell myself.
evals.expected_output: Writes code that selects explicit files from `run_dir` (not the whole scratch tree, which can hold source data and credentials), writes aggregate metrics to a new JSON file with allow_nan=False, builds an archive with the packaged `create_archive` helper from an explicit list of relative paths, uploads with `session.file.put(..., auto_compress=False, overwrite=False)` to a new run-specific prefix and checks exactly one `UPLOADED` result, and records the stage path and archive SHA256 digest.
assertions: The code selects explicit files from one run instead of uploading the whole scratch directory
The code uses the packaged create_archive helper with a list of explicit relative file paths
The code uploads with session.file.put and overwrite=False
The code checks that the upload status is UPLOADED and treats anything else, including SKIPPED, as not retained
The code records the stage object path and the archive digest

evals.prompt: Look up my Kumo model by its hosted job ID job-8841 and redeploy it.
evals.expected_output: The local Kumo API has no hosted model or job ID lookup. It says so and asks for the registry model name and version, or a retained bundle, instead of inventing a lookup.
assertions: Says there is no hosted model or job ID lookup in this local API
Asks for a registry model and explicit version, or a retained bundle
Does not invent an API call that fetches a model by job ID

evals.prompt: Save my trained scikit-learn model with joblib and upload it to s3://ml-models/fraud/.
evals.expected_output: A scikit-learn persistence task unrelated to Kumo. The agent answers with joblib and an S3 upload, without loading the Kumo persistence skill.
assertions: Does not load or follow the kumo-model-persistence skill
Uses joblib to save the model and uploads it to the S3 path
